    MA4704 · AEROELASTICITY

    Structural Dynamics

    #Lagrange’s Equation

    Lagrange’s equation is represented as,

    💡

    L=K−P=T−U

    Function = Kinetic energy - Potential energy

    For a conservative system,

    💡

    dtd​(∂q˙​i​∂L​)−∂qi​∂L​=0

    For a non-conservative system,

    💡

    dtd​(∂q˙​i​∂L​)−∂qi​∂L​=Qi​

    where qi​ represents the generalized coordinates, and Qi′​ represents the generalized forces

    #Example (Pendulum)

    The pendulum rotates about the point O denoted by θ,
    and rotates about the vertical axis passing through O, denoted by ϕ. Thus, vθ​⊥vϕ​.

    Velocity due to rotation about O,

    vθ​=rω=lθ˙

    Velocity due to rotation about vertical axis,

    vϕ​=rω=(lsinθ)ϕ˙​

    Kinetic energy of pendulum,

    K=21​mv2=21​m(v⋅v)

    K=21​m[(vθ​+vϕ​)⋅(vθ​+vϕ​)]

    K=21​m(vθ​⋅vθ​+vθ​⋅vϕ​+vϕ​⋅vθ​+vϕ​⋅vϕ​)

    K=21​m[(vθ​vθ​)cos0°+(vθ​vϕ​)cos90°+(vϕ​vθ​)cos90°+(vϕ​vϕ​)cos0°]

    K=21​m(vθ2​+vϕ2​)

    K=21​ml2(θ˙2+ϕ˙​2sin2θ)

    Potential energy of pendulum,

    P=−mgh

    P=−mg[lcos(π−θ)]

    P=mglcosθ

    Lagrangian function,

    L=K−P

    L=21​ml2(θ˙2+ϕ˙​2sin2θ)−mglcosθ

    Degree of freedom θ,

    dtd​(∂θ˙∂L​)−∂θ∂L​=0

    dtd​(ml2θ˙)−(ml2ϕ˙​2sinθcosθ+mglsinθ)=0

    ml2θ¨−ml2ϕ˙​2sinθcosθ+mglsinθ=0

    Degree of freedom ϕ,

    dtd​(∂ϕ˙​∂L​)−∂ϕ∂L​=0

    dtd​(ml2ϕ˙​sin2θ)=0

    ml2ϕ¨​sin2θ+2ml2ϕ˙​(sinθcosθ)θ˙=0

    Equations of motion,

    0=ml2θ¨−ml2ϕ˙​2sinθcosθ−mglsinθ

    0=ml2ϕ¨​sin2θ+2ml2ϕ˙​(sinθcosθ)θ˙

    #Example (Pulleys)

    Relationship between y-displacements,

    l1​=y1​+y4​ → y4​=l1​−y1​ → y˙​4​=−y˙​1​

    l2​=y2​+y3​ → y3​=l2​−y2​ → y˙​3​=−y˙​2​

    Velocity of each mass,

    v1​=y˙​1​

    v2​=y˙​2​+y˙​4​=y˙​2​−y˙​1​

    v3​=y˙​3​+y˙​4​=−y˙​2​−y˙​1​

    Kinetic energy of system,

    K=21​m1​v1​2+21​m2​v2​2+21​m3​v3​2

    K=21​m1​y˙​1​2+21​m2​(y˙​2​−y˙​1​)2+21​m3​(−y˙​2​−y˙​1​)2

    Potential energy of sytem,

    P=−m1​gy1​−m2​g(y2​+y4​)−m3​g(y3​+y4​)

    P=−m1​gy1​−m2​g(l1​−y1​+y2​)−m3​g(l1​+l2​−y1​−y2​)

    Lagrangian function,

    L=K−P

    L=21​m1​y˙​1​2+21​m2​(y˙​2​−y˙​1​)2+21​m3​(−y˙​2​−y˙​1​)2        +m1​gy1​+m2​g(l1​−y1​+y2​)+m3​g(l1​+l2​−y1​−y2​)

    Degree of freedom y1​,

    ∂y1​∂L​=(m1​−m2​−m3​)g

    ∂y˙​1​∂L​=m1​y˙​1​−m2​(y˙​2​−y˙​1​)+m3​(y˙​2​+y˙​1​)

    dtd​(∂y˙​1​∂L​)=m1​y¨​1​−m2​(y¨​2​−y¨​1​)+m3​(y¨​2​+y¨​1​)

    dtd​(∂y˙​1​∂L​)=(m1​+m2​+m3​)y¨​1​+(m2​+m3​)y¨​2​

    Degree of freedom y2​,

    ∂y2​∂L​=m2​g−m3​g

    ∂y˙​2​∂L​=m2​(y˙​2​−y˙​1​)+m3​(y˙​2​+y˙​1​)

    dtd​(∂y˙​2​∂L​)=m2​(y¨​2​−y¨​1​)+m3​(y¨​2​+y¨​1​)

    dtd​(∂y˙​2​∂L​)=(m3​−m2​)y¨​1​+(m2​+m3​)y¨​2​

    Equations of motion,

    0=(m1​+m2​+m3​)y¨​1​+(m2​+m3​)y¨​2​−(m1​−m2​−m3​)g

    0=(m3​−m2​)y¨​1​+(m2​+m3​)y¨​2​−(m2​−m3​)g

    #Example (Beam)

    Vibration response of beam,

    ν(y)=qsin(lπy​)

    ν˙(y)=qsin(lπy​)

    Note that only q is a function of time t.

    Kinetic energy of beam,

    K=21​∫01​ρA(∂t∂ν​)2 dy

    K=21​∫01​ρAq˙​2sin2(lπy​) dy

    K=21​∫01​q˙​2sin2(πy) dy

    K=2q˙​2​∫01​21−cos(2πy)​ dy

    K=2q˙​2​[2y​−4πsin(2πy)​]01​

    K=4q˙​2​

    Potential energy of beam,

    P=21​∫01​EI(∂y2∂2ν​)2 dy

    P=21​∫01​EI[−π2qsin(πy)]2 dy

    P=21​∫01​200π4q2sin2(πy) dy

    P=100π4q2∫01​21−cos(2πy)​ dy

    P=100π4q2[2y​−4πsin(2πy)​]01​

    P=50π4q2

    Lagrangian function,

    L=K−P

    L=4q˙​2​−50π4q2

    dtd​(∂q˙​∂L​)−∂q∂L​=0

    dtd​(2q˙​​)−(−100π4q)=0

    21​q¨​+100π4q=0

    q¨​+200π4q=0

    Performing Laplace transform,

    s2+200π4=0

    ωn2​=200π4

    ωn​=14.142π2 rad/s

    #Uniform String Dynamics

    Consider a string with the following assumptions:

    • Constant tension T in the string
    • Small deformation along vertical axis and slope
    • Negligible gravitational force acting on the string
    • Uniform string stretched between 2 fixed boundaries

    Summation of horizontal forces,

    ∑Fx​=0

    0=T2​cosβ−T1​cosα

    T1​cosα=T2​cosβ=T     [1]

    As there is no motion in the horizontal axis, the x-components of tension must
    remain constant and equal to the initial tension     T in the string during vibration.

    Summation of vertical forces,

    ∑Fy​=may​

    ρΔx∂t2∂2ν​=T2​sinβ−T1​sinα     [2]

    where ρ is expressed in kg/m

    Dividing [2] by [1],

    TρΔx​∂t2∂2ν​=T2​cosβT2​sinβ​−T1​cosαT1​sinα​

    TρΔx​∂t2∂2ν​=tanβ−tanα

    TρΔx​∂t2∂2ν​=∂x∂ν​​x+Δx​−∂x∂ν​​x​

    TρΔx​∂t2∂2ν​=∂x2∂2ν​Δx

    Wave equation that governs the dynamic behavior of the string.

    💡

    ∂x2∂2ν​=Tρ​∂t2∂2ν​

    #Free Vibration

    Boundary conditions:

    1. ν(0,t)=0 (LHS fixed end)
    2. ν(l,t)=0 (RHS fixed end)

    Initial conditions:

    1. ν(x,0)=f(x) (Initial displacement)
    2. ν˙(x,0)=g(x) (Initial velocity)

    Using Separation of Variables method,

    ν(x,t)=X(x)Y(t)

    ∂x2∂2ν​=X′′(x)Y(t)

    ∂t2∂2ν​=X(x)Y¨(t)

    where X(x)= mode shape, Y(t)= amplitude

    Rewriting the wave equation,

    X′′(x)Y(t)=Tρ​⋅X(x)Y¨(t)

    X(x)X′′(x)​=Tρ​Y(t)Y¨(t)​=−α2

    where −α2 is a constant

    From the above, 2 equations of motion can be obtained.

    💡

    X′′(x)+α2⋅X(x)=0

    💡

    Y¨(t)+ρT​α2⋅Y(t)=0

    #Natural Frequencies & Mode Shapes

    Solutions to the 2nd ODE are,

    X(x)=Asin(αx)+Bcos(αx)

    Y(t)=Csin(ρT​​αt)+Dcos(ρT​​αt)

    From the boundary conditions,

    ν(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    ν(l,t)=X(l)Y(t)=0   →   X(l)=0

    Note that amplitude Y(t) cannot be zero (no vibration) at all times.

    Substituting the boundary conditions into X(x),

    X(0)=Asin0+Bcos0   →   B=0

    X(l)=Asin(αl)   →   sin(αl)=0   →   αi​=liπ​ (i=1,2,…)

    Note that A=0 as it would give the trivial solution to mode shape X(x).

    For each value of αi​,

    νi​(x,t)=Xi​(x)Yi​(t)

    νi​(x,t)=Ai​sin(αi​x)[Ci​sin(ρT​​αi​t)+Di​cos(ρT​​αi​t)]

    General equation to describe free vibration response of the string.

    💡

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ei​sin(ρT​​liπ​t)+Fi​cos(ρT​​liπ​t)]

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ei​sin(ωi​t)+Fi​cos(ωi​t)]

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(x)ζi​(t)

    where ωi​= i-th natural frequency, ϕi​(x)= i-th mode shape,
    and     ζi​(t)= harmonic vibration of i-th generalized coordinate

    #Orthogonality of Mode Shapes

    A property of mode shapes is its orthogonality.

    Orthogonality implies the dot product of any two different mode shapes equals zero.
    Each mode shape represents a unique & independent vibration pattern of the system.

    💡

    ∫0l​ ϕi​(x)ϕj​(x) dx=0

    The above applies for i=j.

    💡

    ∫0l​ ϕi​(x)ϕj​(x) dx=2l​

    The above applies for i=j.

    Substituting the 1st initial condition v(x,t)=f(x) into the general equation,

    f(x)=ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ei​sin(ρT​​liπ​t)+Fi​cos(ρT​​liπ​t)]

    f(x)=ν(x,0)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ei​sin0+Fi​cos0)

    f(x)=ν(x,0)=i=1∑∞​ Fi​sin(liπx​)

    Multiplying the above by sin(ljπx​) and integrating from 0 to l,

    ∫0l​ f(x)sin(ljπx​) dx=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ Fi​sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    ∫0l​ f(x)sin(ljπx​) dx=∫0l​ F1​sin(l1πx​)sin(ljπx​)                                             +F2​sin(l2πx​)sin(ljπx​)                                             +⋯+Fj​sin(ljπx​)sin(ljπx​)+… dx

    ∫0l​ f(x)sin(ljπx​) dx=Fj​⋅2l​

    💡

    Fj​=l2​∫0l​ f(x)sin(ljπx​) dx (j=1,2,3,…)

    Substituting the 2nd initial condition ν˙(x,0)=g(x) into the general equation,

    g(x)=ν˙(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ ρT​​liπ​sin(liπx​)[Ei​cos(ρT​​liπ​t)−Fi​sin(ρT​​liπ​t)]

    g(x)=ν˙(x,0)=i=1∑∞​ ρT​​liπ​sin(liπx​)(Ei​cos0−Fi​sin0)

    g(x)=ν˙(x,0)=i=1∑∞​ Ei​ρT​​liπ​sin(liπx​)

    Multiplying the above by sin(ljπx​) and integrating from 0 to l,

    ∫0l​ g(x)sin(ljπx​) dx=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ Ei​ρT​​liπ​sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    ∫0l​ g(x)sin(ljπx​) dx=∫0l​ E1​ρT​​l1π​sin(l1πx​)sin(ljπx​)                                             +E2​ρT​​l2π​sin(l2πx​)sin(ljπx​)                                             +⋯+Ej​ρT​​ljπ​sin(ljπx​)sin(ljπx​)+… dx

    ∫0l​ g(x)sin(ljπx​) dx=Ej​ρT​​2jπ​

    💡

    Ej​=jπ2​Tρ​​∫0l​ g(x)sin(ljπx​) dx (j=1,2,3,…)

    #Forced Vibration

    To describe forced vibration response of the string, we use Lagrange’s equation.

    L=K(ζ˙​)−P(ζ)

    Θi​(t)=dtd​(∂ζ˙​∂L​)−∂ζ∂L​

    where generalized force Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(x,t)ϕi​(x) dx

    Free vibration response of the string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(x)ζi​(t)

    Kinetic energy of the system,

    K=∫0l​ 21​ρ(∂t∂ν​)2 dx

    K=∫0l​ 21​ρ[i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(x)ζ˙​i​(t)]2 dx

    K=2ρ​∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ j=1∑∞​ ϕi​(x)ζ˙​i​(t)ϕj​(x)ζ˙​j​(t) dx

    K=2ρ​[i=1∑∞​ j=1∑∞​ ζ˙​i​(t)ζ˙​j​(t)][∫0l​ ϕi​(x)ϕj​(x) dx]

    💡

    K=4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ζ˙​i​2(t)

    Potential energy of the system,

    P=∫0l​ 21​T(∂x∂ν​)2 dx

    P=∫0l​ 21​T[i=1∑∞​ ϕi′​(x)ζi​(t)]2 dx

    P=2T​∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ j=1∑∞​ ϕi′​(x)ζi​(t)ϕj′​(x)ζj​(t) dx

    P=2T​[i=1∑∞​ j=1∑∞​ ζi​(t)ζj​(t)][∫0l​ ϕi′​(x)ϕj′​(x) dx]

    P=2T​i=1∑∞​ ζi​2(t)⋅∫0l​ ϕi′​2(x) dx

    P=2T​i=1∑∞​ ζi​2(t)⋅∫0l​ (liπ​cosliπx​)2 dx

    P=2T​i=1∑∞​ ζi​2(t)⋅l2i2π2​2l​

    P=4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ρT​l2i2π2​⋅ζi​2(t)

    💡

    P=4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ωi​2ζi​2(t)

    Applying Lagrange’s equation,

    L=4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ζ˙​i​2(t)−4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ωi​2ζi​2(t)

    ∂ζ˙​∂L​=∂ζ˙​∂​[4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ζ˙​i​2(t)]=2ρl​⋅ζ˙​i​(t)

    ∂ζ∂L​=∂ζ∂​[−4ρl​i=1∑∞​ ωi​2ζi​2(t)]=−2ρl​⋅ωi​2ζi​(t)

    💡

    Θi​(t)=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t) (i=1,2,3,…)

    #Vibration Examples

    #Example 1 (Initial Displacement)

    #Part (i)

    Natural frequencies,

    ωi​=ρT​​liπ​=0.01100​​1iπ​=100iπ

    ω1,2,3​=100π, 200π, 300π rad/s

    #Part (ii)

    Mode shapes,

    ϕi​=sinliπx​=sin(iπx)

    ϕ1,2,3​=sin(πx), sin(2πx), sin(3πx)

    #Part (iii)

    Boundary conditions,

    ν(x=0,t)=0 (RHS fixed end)

    ν(x=l,t)=0 (LHS fixed end)

    Initial conditions,

    ν(x,0)=f(x) (Initial displacement)

    ν˙(x,0)=g(x)=0 (Initial velocity)

    From the diagram, function to describe initial displacement,

    f(x)={0.02x0.02(1−x)​0≤x≤0.50.5≤x≤1​

    Equations are obtained using y=mx+c.

    General equation for free vibration response,

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ei​sin(ωi​t)+Fi​cos(ωi​t)]

    Ej​=jπ2​Tρ​​∫0l​ g(x)sin(ljπx​) dx

    Fj​=l2​∫0l​ f(x)sin(ljπx​) dx

    Since initial velocity is zero, g(x)=0, and thus Ej​=0.

    Solving for coefficient Fj​,

    Fj​=12​[∫00.5​ 0.02xsin(jπx) dx+∫0.51​ 0.02(1−x)sin(jπx) dx]

    Fj​=0.04[∫00.5​ xsin(jπx) dx+∫0.51​ (1−x)sin(jπx) dx]

    Fj​=0.04[(jπ)22​sin(0.5jπ)]

    Fj​=(jπ)20.08​sin2jπ​

    Fj​={(jπ)20.08​(−1)(j−1)/20​j=1,3,5,…j=2,4,6,…​

    Integration by parts

    ∫uv′ dx=uv−∫vu′ dx

    u=x and v′=sin(jπx)

    u′=1 and v=−jπcos(jπx)​

    ∫uv′ dx=uv−∫vu′ dx

    u=1−x and v′=sin(jπx)

    u′=−1 and v=−jπcos(jπx)​

    ∫00.5​ xsin(jπx) dx

    =[−jπxcos(jπx)​]00.5​−∫00.5​ −jπcos(jπx)​ dx

    =[−jπxcos(jπx)​+(jπ)2sin(jπx)​]00.5​

    =−jπ0.5​cos(0.5jπ)+(jπ)21​sin(0.5jπ)

    ∫0.51​ (1−x)sin(jπx) dx

    =[−jπ(1−x)cos(jπx)​]0.51​−∫0.51​ jπcos(jπx)​ dx

    =[−jπ(1−x)cos(jπx)​−(jπ)2sin(jπx)​]0.51​

    =jπ0.5​cos(0.5jπ)+(jπ)21​sin(0.5jπ)

    Vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(iπx)[(iπ)20.08​(−1)(i−1)/2cos(100iπt)]

    #Example 2 (Distributed Load)

    Generalized force,

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(x,t)ϕi​(x) dx

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F0​sin(ωt)sin(liπx​) dx

    Θi​(t)=F0​sin(ωt)[−(iπ/l)cos(iπx/l)​]0l​

    Θi​(t)=iπF0​lsin(ωt)​[−cos(iπ)+cos0]

    Θi​(t)={iπ2F0​l​sin(ωt)0​i=1,3,5,…i=2,4,6,…​

    Equation of motion,

    Θi​(t)=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)

    iπ2F0​l​sin(ωt)=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)

    Note that the EoM is a non-homogeneous 2nd ODE.
    Its general solution contains two parts — homogeneous and particular.
    Homogeneous solution is the free vibration, particular is the forced vibration.

    Solving 2nd ODE

    Homogeneous solution,

    ζi,h​(t)=Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)

    Homogeneous solution can be obtained by equating external forces to zero.

    Assume forced vibration response to be ζi,p​(t)=Ap​sin(ωt).

    ζ˙​i,p​(t)=Ap​ωcos(ωt)

    ζ¨​i,p​(t)=−Ap​ω2sin(ωt)

    Substituting the above into the EoM,

    iπ2F0​l​sin(ωt)=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)

    iπ2F0​l​sin(ωt)=−2ρl​Ap​ω2sin(ωt)+2ρl​ωi​2Ap​sin(ωt)

    iρπ4F0​​=−Ap​ω2+Ap​ωi​2

    Ap​=iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​​

    Particular solution,

    ζi,p​(t)=iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​​sin(ωt)

    General solution to equation of motion,

    ζi​(t)=Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​​sin(ωt)

    Coefficient Bi​

    Forced vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ ϕi​(x)ζi​(t)

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​​sin(ωt)]

    Assume the 1st initial condition to be ν(x,0)=0.

    0=i=1,3,5∑∞​ Bi​sin(liπx​)

    Using the orthogonality principle,

    0=∫0l​ ∑ Bi​sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    0=Bi​⋅2l​

    Bi​=0

    Coefficient Ai​

    Forced vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​​sin(ωt)]

    ν˙(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​ωi​cos(ωi​t)+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​ω​cos(ωt)]

    Assume the 2nd initial condition to be ν˙(x,0)=0.

    0=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​ωi​+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​ω​]

    Using the orthogonality principle,

    0=∫0l​ ∑[Ai​ωi​+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​ω​]sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    0=2l​[Ai​ωi​+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​ω​]

    Ai​=−iρπωi​(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​ω​

    Forced vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[−iρπωi​(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​ω​sin(ωi​t)+iρπ(ωi​2−ω2)4F0​​sin(ωt)]

    ν(x,t)=ρπ4F0​​i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[i(ωi​2−ω2)sin(ωt)​−iωi​(ωi​2−ω2)ωsin(ωi​t)​]

    ν(x,t)=ρπ4F0​​i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[iωi​(ωi​2−ω2)ωi​sin(ωt)−ωsin(ωi​t)​]

    When ω→ωi​, resonance occurs.

    ω → ωi​lim​iωi​(ωi​2−ω2)ωi​sin(ωt)−ωsin(ωi​t)​=ω → ωi​lim​−2iωi​ωωi​tcos(ωt)−sin(ωi​t)​ (L’ Hopital’s Rule)

    ω → ωi​lim​iωi​(ωi​2−ω2)ωi​sin(ωt)−ωsin(ωi​t)​=ω → ωi​lim​−2iωi​−ωi​t2sin(ωt)​ (L’ Hopital’s Rule)

    ω → ωi​lim​iωi​(ωi​2−ω2)ωi​sin(ωt)−ωsin(ωi​t)​=2iωi​ωi​t2sin(ωi​t)​

    Response tends to infinity as t↑.

    #Example 3 (Concentrated Load)

    Generalized force,

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(x,t)ϕi​(x) dx

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ Fc​(t)δ(x−xc​)ϕi​(x) dx

    Θi​(t)=Fc​(t)ϕi​(xc​)

    Θi​(t)=F0​(sinliπx​)x=xc​=l/2​

    Θi​(t)=F0​sin2iπ​

    Θi​(t)={F0​(−1)(i−1)/20​i=1,3,5,…i=2,4,6,…​

    Equation of motion,

    Θi​(t)=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)

    F0​(−1)(i−1)/2=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)

    ρl2F0​​(−1)(i−1)/2=2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)

    When i is odd, 2nd ODE is non-homogeneous.
    When     i is even, 2nd ODE is homogeneous.

    General solutions to equation of motion,

    ζi​(t)=Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+Ci​

    Coefficient Ci​

    Let the particular solution be ζi,p​(t)=Ci​.

    Substituting into the equation of motion,

    ζ¨​i​(t)+ωi​2ζi​(t)=ρl2F0​​(−1)(i−1)/2

    0+ωi​2Ci​=ρl2F0​​(−1)(i−1)/2

    Ci​=i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2

    Coefficient Ai​

    Forced vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2]                +i=2,4,6∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)]

    ν˙(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​ωi​cos(ωi​t)−Bi​ωi​sin(ωi​t)]                +i=2,4,6∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​ωi​cos(ωi​t)−Bi​ωi​sin(ωi​t)]

    Assume the 1st initial condition to be ν˙(x,0)=0.

    0=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​ωi​cos0−Bi​ωi​sin0]       +i=2,4,6∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Ai​ωi​cos0−Bi​ωi​sin0]

    0=i=1,3,5∑∞​ Ai​ωi​sin(liπx​)+i=2,4,6∑∞​ Ai​ωi​sin(liπx​)

    Using the orthogonality principle,

    0=∫0l​ i=1,3,5∑∞​ Ai​ωi​sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​)+i=2,4,6∑∞​ Ai​ωi​sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    0=Ai​ωi​l

    Ai​=0

    Coefficient Bi​

    Forced vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Bi​cos(ωi​t)+i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2]                +i=2,4,6∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Bi​cos(ωi​t)]

    2nd initial condition is given as ν(x,0)=hsinl4π​.

    ν(x,0)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Bi​cos0+i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2]                 +i=2,4,6∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Bi​cos0]

    hsinl4π​=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sin(liπx​)[Bi​+i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2]+i=2,4,6∑∞​ Bi​sin(liπx​)

    Using the orthogonality principle,

    ∫0l​ hsin(l4π​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    =∫0l​ i=1,3,5∑∞​ [Bi​+i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2]sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​)          +i=2,4,6∑∞​ Bi​sin(liπx​)sin(ljπx​) dx

    →⎩⎨⎧​0=2l​[Bi​+i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2]0=Bi​2l​h2l​=B4​2l​​j=i (odd)j=i (even), i=4j=i=4​

    →⎩⎨⎧​Bi​=−i2π2T2F0​l​(−1)(i−1)/2Bi​=0B4​=h​i=Oddi=Even, i=4i=4​

    Forced vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ sinliπx​[i2π2T2F0​l(−1)(i−1)/2(1−cosωi​t)​]+hsinl4πx​cosω4​t

    #Example 4 (Combination Load)

    Generalized force,

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(x,t)ϕi​(t) dx

    Θi​(t)=Fc​(t)ϕi​(xc​)+∫0l​ q0​[1−sin(l3πx​)]sinΩtsin(liπx​) dx

    Θi​(t)=F0​sinΩtsin(2iπ​)+q0​sinΩt∫0l​ sin(liπx​)−sin(l3πx​)sin(liπx​) dx

    Θi​(t)=F0​sinΩtsin(2iπ​)+iπq0​l​[1−cos(iπ)]sinΩt−2q0​l​⋅δ(i−3)sinΩt

    Θi​(t)=[F0​sin2iπ​+iπq0​l​(1−cosiπ)−2q0​l​δ(i−3)]sinΩt

    Integration

    ∫0l​ sin(liπx​)−sin(l3πx​)sin(liπx​) dx

    =[−iπl​cos(liπx​)]0l​−∫0l​ sin(l3πx​)sin(liπx​) dx

    =iπl​[1−cos(iπ)]−2l​⋅δ(i−3)

    Note that the 2nd term is in the form ∫0l​ ϕi​(x)ϕj​(x) dx.
    If     i=j, the result of the integral is zero. If i=j, the result of the integral is l/2.
    Thus, we can express it as an impulse function where     δ(i−3)=1 when i=3.

    Equation of motion,

    2ρl​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)=Θi​(t)

    ζ¨​i​(t)+ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)=F(i)ρl2​[F0​sin2iπ​+iπq0​l​(1−cosiπ)−2q0​l​δ(i−3)]​​sinΩt

    Observations of function F(i),

    F(i)=⎩⎨⎧​0ρl2F0​​(−1)(i−1)/2+iρπ4q0​​−ρl2F0​​+3ρπ4qo​​−ρq0​​​i=Eveni=Odd, i=3i=3​

    Assume the particular solution to be ζi,p​(t)=Ap​sinΩt.

    F(i)sinΩt=−Ap​Ω2sinΩt+Ap​ωi​2sinΩt

    F(i)sinΩt=Ap​(ωi​2−Ω2)sinΩt

    Ap​=ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​

    General solution to 2nd ODE,

    ζi​(t)=Ai​sinωi​t+Bi​cosωi​t+ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​sinΩt

    Vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ai​sinωi​t+Bi​cosωi​t+ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​sinΩt)

    Assume the 1st initial condition to be ν(x,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ai​sin0+Bi​cos0+ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​sin0)

    0=i=1∑∞​ Bi​sin(liπx​)

    Bi​=0

    Vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ai​sinωi​t+ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​sinΩt)

    ν˙(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ai​ωi​cosωi​t+ωi​2−Ω2ΩF(i)​cosΩt)

    Assume the 2nd initial condition to be ν˙(x,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ai​ωi​cos0+ωi​2−Ω2ΩF(i)​cos0)

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−Ω2ΩF(i)​)

    0=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ (Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−Ω2ΩF(i)​)sin(liπx​)sin(liπj​) dx

    0=2l​(Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−Ω2ΩF(i)​)

    Ai​=−ωi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ΩF(i)​

    Vibration response of string,

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπx​)(−ωi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ΩF(i)​sinωi​t+ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​sinΩt)

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑∞​ ωi​2−Ω2F(i)​sin(liπx​)(sinΩt−ωi​Ω​sinωi​t)

    #Uniform Beam Torsional Dynamics

    Assumptions for pure torsion:

    • Uniform cross-section
    • Homogeneous material properties
    • Center of gravity coincides with elastic axis to decouple torsion and bending

    Summation of torque,

    ∑T=Iα

    (T+∂y∂T​δy)−T=ρIP​δy⋅∂t2∂2θ​

    ∂y∂T​=ρIP​∂t2∂2θ​=[∬A​ ρ(x2+z2) dA]∂t2∂2θ​

    Torsional vibration equation that governs the dynamic behavior of the beam.

    💡

    GIP​∂y2∂2θ​=ρIP​∂t2∂2θ​

    where ρ is expressed in kg/m3, shear modulus G and polar moment of inertia IP​

    Using Separation of Variables,

    θ(y,t)=X(y)Y(t)

    ∂y2∂2θ​=X′′(y)Y(t)

    ∂t2∂2θ​=X(y)Y¨(t)

    Rewriting the torsional vibration equation,

    GIP​⋅X′′(y)Y(t)=ρIP​⋅X(y)Y¨(t)

    X(y)X′′(y)​=Gρ​Y(t)Y¨(t)​=−α2

    where −α2 is a constant

    From the above, 2 equations of motion can be obtained.

    💡

    X′′(y)+α2⋅X(y)=0

    💡

    Y¨(t)+ρG​α2⋅Y(t)=0

    Solutions to the 2nd ODE are,

    X(y)=Asin(αy)+Bcos(αy)

    Y(t)=Csin(ρG​​αt)+Dcos(ρG​​αt)

    #Boundary Conditions

    #Clamped-Clamped

    Boundary conditions:

    1. θ(0,t)=0 (RHS fixed end)
    2. θ(l,t)=0 (LHS fixed end)

    From the boundary conditions,

    θ(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    θ(l,t)=X(l)Y(t)=0   →   X(l)=0

    Substituting the boundary conditions into X(y),

    X(0)=Asin0+Bcos0   →   B=0

    X(l)=Asin(αl)   →   sin(αl)=0   →   αi​=liπ​ (i=1,2,…)

    General equation to describe torsional vibration response of the beam.

    💡

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπy​)[Ei​sin(ρG​​liπ​t)+Fi​cos(ρG​​liπ​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπy​)[Ei​sin(ωi​t)+Fi​cos(ωi​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(y)ζi​(t)

    #Free-Free

    Boundary conditions:

    1. θ′(0,t)=0
    2. θ′(l,t)=0

    No torque applied at both ends.

    From the boundary conditions,

    θ′(0,t)=X′(0)Y(t)=0   →   X′(0)=0

    θ′(l,t)=X′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′(l)=0

    Substituting the boundary conditions into X(y),

    X′(0)=Aαcos0−Bαsin0   →   A=0

    X′(l)=−Bαsin(αl)   →   sin(αl)=0   →   αi​=liπ​ (i=0,1,2,…)

    Note that i=0 exists due to the rigid body mode such that ϕ0​(y)=cos0=1.

    General equation to describe torsional vibration response of the beam.

    💡

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ cos(liπy​)[Ei​sin(ρG​​liπ​t)+Fi​cos(ρG​​liπ​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ cos(liπy​)[Ei​sin(ωi​t)+Fi​cos(ωi​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(y)ζi​(t)

    #Vibration Examples

    #Example 1 : Clamped-Free (Initial Angle of Twist)

    Boundary conditions:

    1. θ(0,t)=0 (Clamped end)
    2. θ′(l,t)=0 (Free end)

    No torque applied at free end,

    T(l)=GIP​∂y∂θ(l.t)​

    0=GIP​⋅θ′(l,t)

    From the boundary conditions,

    θ(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    θ′(l,t)=X′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′(l)=0

    Note that amplitude Y(t) cannot be zero (no vibration) at all times.

    Substituting the boundary conditions into X(y),

    X(0)=Asin0+Bcos0   →   B=0

    X′(l)=Aαcos(αl)   →   cos(αl)=0   →   αi​=2l(2i−1)π​ (i=1,2,…)

    For each value of αi​,

    θi​(y,t)=Xi​(y)Yi​(t)

    θi​(y,t)=Ai​sin(αi​y)+[Ci​sin(ρG​​αi​t)+Di​cos(ρG​​αi​t)]

    General equation to describe free torsional vibration response of the beam.

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ei​sin(ρG​​2l(2i−1)π​t)+Fi​cos(ρG​​2l(2i−1)π​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ei​sin(ωi​t)+Fi​cos(ωi​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ Xi​(y)Yi​(t)

    Initial displacement condition due to applied torque,

    θ(l,0)=GIP​Tl​l​=G(πd4/32)Tl​l​=(9×1010)[π(0.1)4/32]9000(1)​=0.010186 rad

    Initial conditions:

    1. θ(y,0)=0.010186y (Angle of twist varies along beam length)
    2. θ˙(y,0)=0 (Assume zero initial velocity)

    Substituting the 1st initial condition into θ(y,t),

    0.010186y=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​(Ei​sin0+Fi​cos0)

    0.010186y=i=1∑∞​ Fi​sin2l(2i−1)πy​

    Using the orthogonality principle,

    ∫0l​ 0.010186ysin2l(2j−1)π​ dy=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ Fi​sin2l(2i−1)πy​sin2l(2j−1)πy​ dy

    ∫0l​ 0.010186ysin2l(2j−1)πy​ dy=Fi​2l​

    Fi​=(2j−1)2π20.081488l​sin2(2j−1)π​

    Fi​=(2j−1)2π20.081488l​(−1)j+1

    Integration by parts

    ∫uv′ dy=uv−∫vu′ dy

    u=y and v′=sin2l(2j−1)πy​

    u′=1 and v=−(2j−1)π2l​cos2l(2j−1)πy​

    ∫0l​ ysin2l(2j−1)πy​ dy

    =[−(2j−1)π2ly​cos2l(2j−1)πy​]0l​−∫0l​ −(2j−1)π2l​cos2l(2j−1)πy​ dy

    =−(2j−1)π2l2​cos2(2j−1)π​+[(2j−1)2π24l2​sin2l(2j−1)πy​]0l​

    =(2j−1)2π24l2​sin2(2j−1)π​

    Substituting the 2nd initial condition into θ˙(y,t),

    θ˙(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ei​ωi​cos(ωi​t)−Fi​ωi​sin(ωi​t)]

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ei​ωi​cos0−Fi​ωi​sin0]

    0=i=1∑∞​ Ei​ωi​sin2l(2i−1)πy​

    Using the orthogonality principle,

    0=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ Ei​ωi​sin2l(2i−1)πy​sin2l(2j−1)πy​ dy

    0=Ei​ωi​2l​

    Ei​=0

    Free torsional vibration response of beam,

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ei​sin(ρG​​2l(2i−1)π​t)+Fi​cos(ρG​​2l(2i−1)π​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[(2i−1)2π20.081488l​(−1)i+1cos(ρG​​2l(2i−1)π​t)]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2(2j−1)πy​{(2i−1)2π20.081488(−1)i+1​cos[5335.7(2i−1)t]}

    #Example 2 : Clamped-Free (Combination Torque)

    Generalized force,

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(y,t)ϕi​(y) dy

    Θi​(t)=Fc​(t)ϕi​(yc​)+∫0l​ q(y,t)ϕi​(y) dy

    Θi​(t)=T0​sinΩtsin2(2i−1)π​+∫0l​ q0​sinΩtsin2l(2i−1)πy​ dy

    Θi​(t)=T0​sinΩtsin2(2i−1)π​+q0​sinΩt[−(2i−1)π2l​cos2l(2i−1)πy​]0l​

    Θi​(t)=(−1)i+1T0​sinΩt+(2i−1)π2q0​l​sinΩt

    Θi​(t)=[(−1)i+1T0​+(2i−1)π2q0​l​]sinΩt

    where T0​=5000 Nm, q0​=8000 Nand Ω=2000 rad/s

    Equation of motion,

    2ρl⋅IP​​⋅ζ¨​i​(t)+2ρl⋅IP​​ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)=Θi​(t)

    ζ¨​i​(t)+ωi​2⋅ζi​(t)=T(i)[(−1)i+1T0​+(2i−1)π2q0​l​]​​sinΩt

    General solution to 2nd ODE,

    ζi​(t)=Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+ωi​2−Ω2T(i)​sinΩt

    Torsional vibration response of beam,

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+ωi​2−Ω2T(i)​sinΩt]

    θ˙(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ai​ωi​cos(ωi​t)−Bi​ωi​sin(ωi​t)+ωi​2−Ω2ΩT(i)​cosΩt]

    Assume the 1st initial condition to be θ(y,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ai​sin0+Bi​cos0+ωi​2−Ω2T(i)​sin0]

    0=i=1∑∞​ Bi​sin2l(2i−1)πy​

    Bi​=0

    Assume the 2nd initial condition to be θ˙(y,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ai​ωi​cos0−Bi​ωi​sin0+ωi​2−Ω2ΩT(i)​cos0]

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−Ω2ΩT(i)​]

    0=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ [Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−Ω2ΩT(i)​]sin2l(2i−1)πy​sin2l(2j−1)πy​ dy

    0=[Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−Ω2ΩT(i)​]2l​

    Ai​=−ωi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ΩT(i)​

    Torsional vibration response of beam,

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin2l(2i−1)πy​[−ωi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ΩT(i)​sin(ωi​t)+ωi​2−Ω2T(i)​sinΩt]

    θ(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ ωi​2−Ω2T(i)​sin2l(2i−1)πy​[sinΩt−ωi​Ω​sin(ωi​t)]

    #Uniform Beam Bending Dynamics

    Assumptions for pure bending:

    • Uniform cross-section
    • Homogeneous material properties
    • Center of gravity coincides with elastic axis to decouple torsion and bending
    • External forces act through the shear center such that only bending occurs

    Summation of vertical forces,

    ∑F=ma

    V−(V+∂y∂V​δy)=(ρAδy​)∂t2∂2ν​

    −∂y∂V​=ρA∂t2∂2ν​

    Summation of moments about O,

    ∑M=0

    M+Vδy−(M+∂y∂M​δy)=0

    V=∂y∂M​

    Bending moment is proportional to local curvature,

    ∂y2∂2M​=−ρA∂t2∂2ν​

    ∂y2∂2​(EI∂y2∂2ν​)=−ρA∂t2∂2ν​

    0=EI∂y4∂4ν​+ρA∂t2∂2ν​

    0=ρAEI​∂y4∂4ν​+∂t2∂2ν​

    Bending vibration equation that governs the dynamic behavior of the beam.

    💡

    0=a4∂y4∂4ν​+∂t2∂2ν​

    where a=4EI/ρA​

    Using Separation of Variables,

    ν(y,t)=X(y)Y(t)

    ∂y4∂4ν​=X′′′′(y)Y(t)

    ∂t2∂2ν​=X(y)Y¨(t)

    Rewriting the bending vibration equation,

    0=a4X′′′′(y)Y(t)+X(y)Y¨(t)

    X(y)X′′′′(y)​=−a41​Y(t)Y¨(t)​=α4

    where α4 is a constant

    From the above, 2 equations of motion can be obtained.

    💡

    X′′′′(y)−α4⋅X(y)=0

    General solution to X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)              +D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    💡

    Y¨(t)+a4α4⋅Y(t)=0

    General solution to Y(t),

    Y(t)=Asin(a2α2t)+Bcos(a2α2t)

    ω=a2α2=ρAEI​​α2=(αl)2ρAl4EI​​

    #Boundary Conditions

    List of boundary conditions:

    • ν(y,t)=X(y)Y(t) (Deflection)
    • ν′(y,t)=X′(y)Y(t) (Slope)
    • M(y,t)=EI∂y2∂2ν​=EI⋅X′′(y)Y(t) (Bending moment)
    • V(y,t)=EI∂y3∂3ν​=EI⋅X′′′(y)Y(t) (Shear force)

    Clamped EndFree EndPinned End
    Deflection ν0XY0
    Slope ν′0X′YX′Y
    Bending Moment ν′′EIX′′Y00
    Shear Force ν′′′EIX′′′Y0EIX′′′Y

    #Pinned-Pinned

    The beam is supported by a pivot at each end.

    Boundary conditions at LHS,

    [1]     ν(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    [2]     M(0,t)=EIX′′(0)Y(t)=0   →   X′′(0)=0

    Boundary conditions at RHS,

    [3]     ν(l,t)=X(l)Y(t)=0   →   X(l)=0

    [4]     M(l,t)=EIX′′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′′(l)=0

    Substituting [1] into the general solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(0)=D1​cosh0+D2​sinh0+D3​cos0+D4​sin0

    0=D1​+D3​

    D3​=−D1​

    Substituting [2] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′(y)=α2D1​cosh(αy)+α2D2​sinh(αy)−α2D3​cos(αy)−α2D4​sin(αy)

    X′′(0)=α2D1​cosh0+α2D2​sinh0−α2D3​cos0−α2D4​sin0

    0=α2D1​−α2D3​

    D1​=D3​

    Substituting [3] into the general solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D2​sinh(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(l)=D2​sinh(αl)+D4​sin(αl)

    0=D2​sinh(αl)+D4​sin(αl)

    Substituting [4] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′(y)=α2D2​sinh(αy)−α2D4​sin(αy)

    X′′(l)=α2D2​sinh(αl)−α2D4​sin(αl)

    0=D2​sinh(αl)−D4​sin(αl)

    Writing in matrix form,

    💡

    {00​}=[sinh(αl)sinh(αl)​sin(αl)−sin(αl)​]{D2​D4​​}

    Determinant of matrix,

    0=det​sinh(αl)sinh(αl)​sin(αl)−sin(αl)​​

    0=−2sinh(αl)sin(αl)

    0=sin(αl)

    💡

    αi​l=iπ

    where i=1,2,3,…

    Substituting into the original matrix,

    {00​}=[sinh(αi​l)sinh(αi​l)​00​]{D2​D4​​}

    0=D2​sinh(αi​l)

    D2​=0

    General solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D4​sin(αi​y)

    Bending vibration mode shapes of the beam is,

    💡

    ϕi​(y)=sin(liπy​)

    where i=1,2,3,…

    #Clamped-Free

    The beam is clamped at the LHS and free at the RHS.

    Boundary conditions at LHS,

    [1]     ν(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    [2]     ν′(0,t)=X′(0)Y(t)   →   X′(0)=0

    Boundary conditions at RHS,

    [3]     M(l,t)=EIX′′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′′(l)=0

    [4]     V(l,t)=EIX′′′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′′′(l)=0

    Substituting [1] into the general solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(0)=D1​cosh0+D2​sinh0+D3​cos0+D4​sin0

    0=D1​+D3​

    D3​=−D1​

    Substituting [2] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′(y)=αD1​sinh(αy)+αD2​cosh(αy)−αD3​sin(αy)+αD4​cos(αy)

    X′(0)=αD1​sinh0+αD2​cosh0−αD3​sin0+αD4​cos0

    0=D2​+D4​

    D4​=−D2​

    Substituting [3] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′(y)=α2D1​cosh(αy)+α2D2​sinh(αy)+α2D1​cos(αy)+α2D2​sin(αy)

    X′′(l)=α2D1​cosh(αl)+α2D2​sinh(αl)+α2D1​cos(αl)+α2D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​cosh(αl)+D2​sinh(αl)+D1​cos(αl)+D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)]+D2​[sinh(αl)+sin(αl)]

    Substituting [4] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′′(y)=α3D1​sinh(αy)+α3D2​cosh(αy)−α3D1​sin(αy)+α3D2​cos(αy)

    X′′′(l)=α3D1​sinh(αl)+α3D2​cosh(αl)−α3D1​sin(αl)+α3D2​cos(αl)

    0=D1​sinh(αl)+D2​cosh(αl)−D1​sin(αl)+D2​cos(αl)

    0=D1​[sinh(αl)−sin(αl)]+D2​[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)]

    Writing in matrix form,

    💡

    {00​}=[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)sinh(αl)−sin(αl)​sinh(αl)+sin(αl)cosh(αl)+cos(αl)​]{D1​D2​​}

    Determinant of matrix,

    0=det​cosh(αl)+cos(αl)sinh(αl)−sin(αl)​sinh(αl)+sin(αl)cosh(αl)+cos(αl)​​

    0=[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)]2−sinh2(αl)+sin2(αl)

    0=cosh2(αl)+2cosh(αl)cos(αl)+cos2(αl)−sinh2(αl)+sin2(αl)

    0=2cosh(αl)cos(αl)+2

    💡

    0=cosh(αl)cos(αl)+1

    Substituting known αi​l value into the original matrix,

    0=[cosh(αi​l)+cos(αi​l)]D1​+[sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)]D2​

    0=sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)cosh(αi​l)+cos(αi​l)​D1​+D2​

    0=βi​D1​+D2​

    Define a new parameter βi​ for clamped-free condition.

    💡

    βi,CF​=sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)cosh(αi​l)+cos(αi​l)​

    General solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)−βD1​sinh(αy)−D1​cos(αy)+βD1​sin(αy)

    X(y)=D1​[cosh(αy)−βsinh(αy)−cos(αy)+βsin(αy)]

    Bending vibration mode shapes of the beam is,

    💡

    ϕi​(y)=cosh(αi​y)−βsinh(αi​y)−cos(αi​y)+βsin(αi​y)

    #Free-Free

    The beam is free at both ends.

    Boundary conditions at LHS,

    [1]     ν′′(0,t)=EIX′′(0)Y(t)=0   →   X′′(0)=0

    [2]     ν′′′(0,t)=EIX′′′(0)Y(t)=0   →   X′′′(0)=0

    Boundary conditions at RHS,

    [3]     ν′′(l,t)=EIX′′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′′(l)=0

    [4]     ν′′′(l,t)=EIX′′′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′′′(l)=0

    Substituting [1] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′(y)=α2D1​cosh(αy)+α2D2​sinh(αy)−α2D3​cos(αy)−α2D4​sin(αy)

    X′′(0)=α2D1​cosh0+α2D2​sinh0−α2D3​cos0−α2D4​sin0

    0=D1​−D3​

    D1​=D3​

    Substituting [2] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′′(y)=α3D1​sinh(αy)+α3D2​cosh(αy)+α3D3​sin(αy)−α3D4​cos(αy)

    X′′′(y0)=α3D1​sinh0+α3D2​cosh0+α3D3​sin0−α3D4​cos0

    0=D2​−D4​

    D2​=D4​

    Substituting [3] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′(y)=α2D1​cosh(αy)+α2D2​sinh(αy)−α2D1​cos(αy)−α2D2​sin(αy)

    X′′(l)=α2D1​cosh(αl)+α2D2​sinh(αl)−α2D1​cos(αl)−α2D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​cosh(αl)+D2​sinh(αl)−D1​cos(αl)−D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)]+D2​[sinh(αl)−sin(αl)]

    Substituting [4] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′′(y)=α3D1​sinh(αy)+α3D2​cosh(αy)+α3D1​sin(αy)−α3D2​cos(αy)

    X′′′(l)=α3D1​sinh(αl)+α3D2​cosh(αl)+α3D1​sin(αl)−α3D2​cos(αl)

    0=D1​sinh(αl)+D2​cosh(αl)+D1​sin(αl)−D2​cos(αl)

    0=D1​[sinh(αl)+sin(αl)]+D2​[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)]

    Writing in matrix form,

    💡

    {00​}=[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)sinh(αl)+sin(αl)​sinh(αl)−sin(αl)cosh(αl)−cos(αl)​]{D1​D2​​}

    Determinant of matrix,

    0=det​cosh(αl)−cos(αl)sinh(αl)+sin(αl)​sinh(αl)−sin(αl)cosh(αl)−cos(αl)​​

    0=[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)]2−sinh2(αl)+sin2(αl)

    0=cosh2(αl)−2cosh(αl)cos(αl)+cos2(αl)−sinh2(αl)+sin2(αl)

    0=−2cosh(αl)cos(αl)+2

    💡

    1=cosh(αl)cos(αl)

    Substituting known αi​l value into the original matrix,

    0=[sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)]D1​+[cosh(αi​l)−cos(αi​l)]D2​

    0=cosh(αi​l)−cos(αi​l)sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)​D1​+D2​

    0=βi​D1​+D2​

    Define a new parameter βi​ for free-free condition.

    💡

    βi,FF​=cosh(αi​l)−cos(αi​l)sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)​

    General solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)−βD1​sinh(αy)+D1​cos(αy)−βD1​sin(αy)

    X(y)=D1​[cosh(αy)−βsinh(αy)+cos(αy)−βsin(αy)]

    Bending vibration mode shapes of the beam is,

    💡

    ϕi​(y)=cosh(αi​y)−βsinh(αi​y)+cos(αi​y)−βsin(αi​y)

    #Clamped-Clamped

    The beam is clamped at both ends.

    Boundary conditions at LHS,

    [1]     ν(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    [2]     ν′(0,t)=X′(0)Y(t)=0   →   X′(0)=0

    Boundary conditions at RHS,

    [3]     ν(l,t)=X(l)Y(t)=0   →   X(l)=0

    [4]     ν′(l,t)=X′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′(l)=0

    Substituting [1] into the general solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(0)=D1​cosh0+D2​sinh0+D3​cos0+D4​sin0

    0=D1​+D3​

    D3​=−D1​

    Substituting [2] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′(y)=αD1​sinh(αy)+αD2​cosh(αy)−αD3​sin(αy)+αD4​cos(αy)

    X′(0)=αD1​sinh0+αD2​cosh0−αD3​sin0+αD4​cos0

    0=D2​+D4​

    D4​=−D2​

    Substituting [3] into the general solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)−D1​cos(αy)−D2​sin(αy)

    X(l)=D1​cosh(αl)+D2​sinh(αl)−D1​cos(αl)−D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​cosh(αl)+D2​sinh(αl)−D1​cos(αl)−D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)]+D2​[sinh(αl)−sin(αl)]

    Substituting [4] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′(y)=αD1​sinh(αy)+αD2​cosh(αy)+αD1​sin(αy)−αD2​cos(αy)

    X′(l)=αD1​sinh(αl)+αD2​cosh(αl)+αD1​sin(αl)−αD2​cos(αl)

    0=D1​sinh(αl)+D2​cosh(αl)+D1​sin(αl)−D2​cos(αl)

    0=D1​[sinh(αl)+sin(αl)]+D2​[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)]

    Writing in matrix form,

    💡

    {00​}=[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)sinh(αl)+sin(αl)​sinh(αl)−sin(αl)cosh(αl)−cos(αl)​]{D1​D2​​}

    Determinant of matrix,

    0=det​cosh(αl)−cos(αl)sinh(αl)+sin(αl)​sinh(αl)−sin(αl)cosh(αl)−cos(αl)​​

    0=[cosh(αl)−cos(αl)]2−sinh2(αl)+sin2(αl)

    0=cosh2(αl)−2cosh(αl)cos(αl)+cos2(αl)−sinh2(αl)+sin2(αl)

    0=−2cosh(αl)cos(αl)+2

    💡

    1=cosh(αl)cos(αl)

    Substituting known αi​l value into the original matrix,

    0=[sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)]D1​+[cosh(αi​l)−cos(αi​l)]D2​

    0=cosh(αi​l)−cos(αi​l)sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)​D1​+D2​

    0=βi​D1​+D2​

    Define a new parameter βi​ for clamped-clamped condition.

    💡

    βi,CC​=cosh(αi​l)−cos(αi​l)sinh(αi​l)+sin(αi​l)​

    General solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)−βD1​sinh(αy)−D1​cos(αy)+βD1​sin(αy)

    X(y)=D1​[cosh(αy)−βsinh(αy)−cos(αy)+βsin(αy)]

    Bending vibration mode shapes of the beam is,

    💡

    ϕi​(y)=cosh(αi​y)−βsinh(αi​y)−cos(αi​y)+βsin(αi​y)

    #Inertia Constraints

    The beam is clamped at the LHS and free at the RHS.
    The mass is considered part of the boundary conditions as it is part of the beam.
    At the free end, there is no bending moment but the mass exerts a ↓ shear force.

    Boundary conditions at LHS,

    [1]     ν(0,t)=X(0)Y(t)=0   →   X(0)=0

    [2]     ν′(0,t)=X′(0)Y(t)=0   →   X′(0)=0

    Boundary conditions at RHS,

    [3]     ν′′(l,t)=EIX′′(l)Y(t)=0   →   X′′(l)=0

    [4]     ν′′′(l,t)=μmν¨(l,t)         EIX′′′(l)Y(t)=μm(−ω2)X(l)Y(t)         EIX′′′(l)=−μma4α4X(l)         EIX′′′(l)=−μ(ρAl)(ρAEI​)α4X(l)         X′′′(l)=−μlα4X(l)

    Substituting [1] into the general solution for X(y),

    X(y)=D1​cosh(αy)+D2​sinh(αy)+D3​cos(αy)+D4​sin(αy)

    X(0)=D1​cosh0+D2​sinh0+D3​cos0+D4​sin0

    0=D1​+D3​

    D3​=−D1​

    Substituting [2] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′(y)=αD1​sinh(αy)+αD2​cosh(αy)−αD3​sin(αy)+αD4​cos(αy)

    X′(0)=αD1​sinh0+αD2​cosh0−αD3​sin0+αD4​cos0

    0=D2​+D4​

    D4​=−D2​

    Substituting [3] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′(y)=α2D1​cosh(αy)+α2D2​sinh(αy)+α2D1​cos(αy)+α2D2​sin(αy)

    X′′(l)=α2D1​cosh(αl)+α2D2​sinh(αl)+α2D1​cos(αl)+α2D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​cosh(αl)+D2​sinh(αl)+D1​cos(αl)+D2​sin(αl)

    0=D1​[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)]+D2​[sinh(αl)+sin(αl)]

    Substituting [4] into the general solution for X(y),

    X′′′(y)=α3D1​sinh(αy)+α3D2​cosh(αy)−α3D1​sin(αy)+α3D2​cos(αy)

    X′′′(l)=α3D1​sinh(αl)+α3D2​cosh(αl)−α3D1​sin(αl)+α3D2​cos(αl)

    −μlαX(l)=D1​sinh(αl)+D2​cosh(αl)−D1​sin(αl)+D2​cos(αl)

    where X(l)=D1​cosh(αl)+D2​sinh(αl)−D1​cos(αl)−D2​sin(αl)

    Writing in matrix form,

    💡

    {00​}=[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)E21​​sinh(αl)+sin(αl)E22​​]{D1​D2​​}

    E21​=−μlαcosh(αl)+μlαcos(αl)−sinh(αl)+sin(αl)

    E22​=−μlαsinh(αl)+μlαsin(αl)−cosh(αl)−cos(αl)

    Determinant of matrix,

    0=det​cosh(αl)+cos(αl)E21​​sinh(αl)+sin(αl)E22​​​

    0=E22​[cosh(αl)+cos(αl)]−E21​[sinh(αl)+sin(αl)]

    💡

    0=E22​cosh(αl)−E21​sinh(αl)+E22​cos(αl)−E21​sin(αl)

    #Vibration Examples

    #Example 1 : Pinned-Pinned (Concentrated Force)

    #Part (a)

    Equation for natural frequency,

    ωi​=(αl)2ρAl4EI​​

    ωi​=(iπ)240(2.1×1011)120.1(0.053)​​​

    ωi​=73.951(i2π2)

    Natural frequencies of beam,

    ω1​=729.87 rad/s

    ω2​=2919.5 rad/s

    ω3​=6568.8 rad/s

    ω4​=11678 rad/s

    #Part (b)

    Generalized force,

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(y,t)ϕi​(y) dy=Fc​(t)ϕi​(yc​)

    Θi​(t)=F0​sinΩtsinliπ(l/2)​

    Θi​(t)=F0​sinΩtsin2iπ​ (i=1,3,5,…)

    Equation of motion,

    Θi​(t)=ρAσi​ζ¨​i​+ρAσi​ωi​2ζi​

    where σi​=∫0l​ ϕi​(y)ϕi​(y) dy

    Evaluating σi​,

    σi​=∫0l​ sin(liπy​)sin(liπy​) dy

    σi​=21​∫0l​ 1−cos(l2iπy​) dy

    σi​=2l​

    Substituting into EoM,

    F0​sinΩtsin2iπ​=2ρAl​ζ¨​i​+2ρAlωi​2​ζi​

    400sin(200t)sin2iπ​=20ζ¨​i​+20ωi​2ζi​

    20(−1)2i−1​sin(200t)=ζ¨​i​+ωi​2ζi​

    Assume forced vibration response to be λsin(200t).

    20(−1)2i−1​sin(200t)=−2002λsin(200t)+ωi​2λsin(200t)

    20(−1)2i−1​=−2002λ+ωi​2λ

    λ=ωi​2−200220(−1)(i−1)/2​

    General solution of 2nd ODE,

    ζi​(t)=Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+ωi​2−200220(−1)(i−1)/2​sin(200t)

    Forced vibration response of beam,

    ν(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπy​)[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)+ωi​2−200220(−1)(i−1)/2​sin(200t)]

    Assume the 1st initial condition to be ν(y,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ Bi​sin(liπy​)

    0=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ Bi​sin(liπy​)sin(ljπy​) dy

    0=Bi​2l​

    Bi​=0

    Assume the 2nd initial condition to be ν˙(y,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ sin(liπy​)[Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−20024000(−1)(i−1)/2​]

    0=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ sin(liπy​)sin(ljπy​)[Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−20024000(−1)(i−1)/2​]

    0=21​[Ai​ωi​+ωi​2−20024000(−1)(i−1)/2​]

    Ai​=−ωi​(ωi​2−2002)4000(−1)(i−1)/2​

    Forced vibration response of beam,

    ν(y,t)=i=1,3,5∑∞​ ωi​2−200220(−1)(i−1)/2​sin(liπy​)[sin(200t)−ωi​200​sin(ωi​t)]

    #Example 2 : Clamped-Free (Initial Velocity)

    Vibration response of beam,

    ν(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(y)[Ai​sin(ωi​t)+Bi​cos(ωi​t)]

    where ϕi​(y)=cosh(αi​y)−βsinh(αi​y)−cos(αi​y)+βsin(αi​y)

    Assume the 1st initial condition to be ν(y,0)=0.

    0=i=1∑∞​ Bi​ϕi​(y)

    Bi​=0

    Initial velocity of the beam is zero, except at y=l where it is v0​.

    v0​=i=1∑∞​ Ai​ωi​ϕi​(y)

    ∫0l​ v0​ϕj​(y) dy=∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ Ai​ωi​ϕi​(y)ϕj​(y) dy

    ∫0l​ v0​ϕj​(y) dy=Ai​ωi​∫0l​ i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(y)ϕj​(y) dy

    ∫l−Δl​ v0​ϕi​(y) dy=Ai​ωi​∫0l​ ϕi​(y)ϕi​(y) dy

    v0​ϕi​(l)∫l−Δl​ dy=Ai​ωi​∫0l​ ϕi​(y)ϕi​(y) dy

    v0​ϕi​(l)Δ=Ai​ωi​σi​

    Ai​=ωi​σi​v0​ϕi​(l)​

    Vibration response of beam,

    ν(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ ωi​σi​v0​ϕi​(l)​ϕi​(y)sin(ωi​t)

    #Example 3 : Clamped-Clamped (Concentrated Force)

    Generalized force,

    Θi​(t)=∫0l​ F(y,t)ϕi​(y) dy=Fc​(t)ϕi​(yc​)

    Θi​(t)=F0​sinΩt⋅ϕi​(l/2)

    Equation of motion,

    Θi​(t)=ρAσi​ζ¨​i​+ρAσi​ωi​2ζi​

    ϕi​(l/2)F0​sinΩt=ρAσi​ζ¨​i​+ρAσi​ωi​2ζi​

    ζ¨​i​+ωi​2ζi​=ρAσi​ϕi​(l/2)F0​​sinΩt

    where σi​=∫0l​ ϕi​(y)ϕi​(y) dy

    Assume forced vibration response to be λsinΩt.

    −λΩ2sinΩt+λωi​2sinΩt=ρAσi​ϕi​(l/2)F0​​sinΩt

    λ=ρAσi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ϕi​(l/2)F0​​

    Particular solution of 2nd ODE,

    ζi,p​(t)=ρAσi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ϕi​(l/2)F0​​sinΩt

    Forced vibration response of beam,

    ν(y,t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(y)ζi,p​(t)=i=1∑∞​ ϕi​(y)⋅ρAσi​(ωi​2−Ω2)ϕi​(l/2)F0​​sinΩt

    #The Ritz Method

    For the bending vibration problem of a non-uniform wing, an approximate
    numerical method is used to to compute vibration properties of the wing.

    General equation to describe vibration response of a system.

    ν(x,t)=i=1∑n​ ϕi​(x)ζi​(t)

    Generalized force applied on a system,

    Qi​=∫0l​ ϕi​(y)F(y,t) dy

    where F(y,t)=q(y,t)+F0​(t)δ(y−y0​),
    whereby 1st term represents distributed force,
    and 2nd term represents concentrated force

    Lagrange’s method to obtain the equations of motion.

    💡

    dtd​(∂ζ˙​i​∂K​)+(∂ζi​∂P​)=Qi​

    Kinetic energy is given as,

    K=21​∫0l​ ρA(y)(∂t∂ν​)2 dy

    K=21​∫0l​ ρA(y)[i=1∑n​ ϕi​(y)ζ˙​i​(t)]2 dy

    K=21​∫0l​ ρA(y)[i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ ϕi​(y)ζ˙​i​(t)⋅ϕj​(y)ζ˙​j​(t)] dy

    K=21​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ ζ˙​i​ζ˙​j​∫0l​ ρA(y)ϕi​(y)ϕj​(y) dy

    💡

    K=21​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ aij​ζ˙​i​ζ˙​j​

    where aij​=∫0l​ ρA(y)ϕi​(y)ϕj​(y) dy

    From Lagrange’s equation,

    ∂ζ˙​i​∂K​=∂ζ˙​i​∂​(21​k=1∑n​j=1∑n​ akj​ζ˙​k​ζ˙​j​)

    ∂ζ˙​i​∂K​=21​∂ζ˙​i​∂​(k=1∑n​j=1, j=i∑n​ akj​ζ˙​k​ζ˙​j​)+21​∂ζ˙​i​∂​(k=1∑n​ aki​ζ˙​k​ζ˙​i​)

    ∂ζ˙​i​∂K​=21​∂ζ˙​i​∂​(j=1, j=i∑n​ aij​ζ˙​i​ζ˙​j​)+21​∂ζ˙​i​∂​(k=1, k=i∑n​ aki​ζ˙​k​ζ˙​i​)+21​∂ζ˙​i​∂​(aii​ζ˙​i​ζ˙​i​)

    ∂ζ˙​i​∂K​=21​j=1, j=i∑n​ aij​ζ˙​j​+21​k=1, k=i∑n​ aki​ζ˙​k​+aii​ζ˙​i​

    💡

    ∂ζ˙​i​∂K​=j=1∑n​ aij​ζ˙​j​

    Potential energy is given as,

    P=21​∫0l​ EI(y)(∂y2∂ν2​)2 dy

    P=21​∫0l​ EI(y)[i=1∑n​ ϕi′′​(y)ζi​(t)]2 dy

    P=21​∫0l​ EI(y)[i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ ϕi′′​(y)ζi​(t)⋅ϕj′′​(y)ζj​(t)] dy

    P=21​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ ζi​ζj​∫0l​ EI(y)ϕi′′​(y)ϕj′′​(y) dy

    💡

    P=21​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ bij​ζi​ζj​

    where bij​=∫0l​ EI(y)ϕi′′​(y)ϕj′′​(y) dy

    From Lagrange’s equation,

    ∂ζi​∂P​=∂ζi​∂​(21​i=1∑n​j=1∑n​ bij​ζi​ζj​)

    ∂ζi​∂P​=21​∂ζi​∂​(k=1∑n​j=1, j=i∑n​ bkj​ζk​ζj​)+21​∂ζi​∂​(k=1∑n​ bki​ζk​ζi​)

    ∂ζi​∂P​=21​∂ζ∂​(j=1, j=i∑n​ bij​ζi​ζj​)+21​∂ζi​∂​(k=1, k=i∑n​ bki​ζk​ζi​)+21​∂ζi​∂​(bii​ζi​ζi​)

    ∂ζi​∂P​=21​j=1, j=i∑n​ bij​ζj​+21​k=1, k=i∑n​ bki​ζk​+bii​ζi​

    💡

    ∂ζi​∂P​=j=1∑n​ bij​ζj​

    Substituting into Lagrange’s equation,

    dtd​(j=1∑n​ aij​ζ˙​j​)+j=1∑n​ bij​ζj​=Qi​

    j=1∑n​ aij​ζ¨​j​+j=1∑n​ bij​ζj​=Qi​

    Writing in matrix form,

    💡

    ⎩⎨⎧​00⋮0​⎭⎬⎫​=M​a11​a21​⋮an1​​a12​a22​⋮an2​​……⋱…​a1n​a2n​⋮ann​​​​​⎩⎨⎧​ζ¨​1​ζ¨​2​⋮ζ¨​n​​⎭⎬⎫​+K​b11​b21​⋮bn1​​b12​b22​⋮bn2​​……⋱…​b1n​b2n​⋮bnn​​​​​⎩⎨⎧​ζ1​ζ2​⋮ζn​​⎭⎬⎫​
